meta.name: English
dns.blocked.blockpage-ip: The ISP's DNS points this host to a block-page IP.
dns.blocked.nxdomain: The ISP's DNS says this host does not exist, but it does (NXDOMAIN poisoning).
dns.blocked.bogon-ip: The ISP's DNS returns a private/invalid address for this host.
dns.blocked.cert-mismatch: The ISP's DNS returns an address that does not present a valid certificate for this host.
dns.decisionRedirect: The block page does not show a court decision; it redirects to {url}.
dns.decisionUnavailable: The court decision could not be read: the block-page server did not answer (it answers only some requests).
http.dropped: Plain HTTP to {ip} with Host "{host}" gets no answer, while Host "{alt}" is answered on the same IP: Host-based HTTP block.
http.urlLevel: The same Host answers for "/" but not for "{path}": the block is specific to this URL.
http.hostLevel: The Host does not answer even for "/": the whole host is blocked over plain HTTP.
http.injection: Plain HTTP: the block page was injected in {hits} of {attempts} attempts (it is injected only some of the time).
http.injectionNone: Plain HTTP: no injected block page in {attempts} attempts.
tcp.primaryClosed: Port {port} is not reachable on these IPs but port 80 is: the server may simply not serve this protocol, so this alone is not an IP block.
dns.noARecord: This host has no IPv4 address (it may be IPv6-only); this tool only tests IPv4.
config.unknownKeySuggest: "{path}" is not a known setting; did you mean "{suggestion}"?
dns.noIspAnswer: No ISP DNS server answered, so DNS-level blocking could not be assessed.
dns.hostMissing: This host does not exist (NXDOMAIN from DoH).
dns.dohUnavailable: DoH reference unavailable; using your system's DNS answers instead (lower confidence).
dns.system.hosts: Your /etc/hosts file maps {host} to {ip}; that entry decides what this computer resolves, not DNS.
dns.system.resolver: The DNS this computer uses ({servers}) also returns the blocked answer.
dns.system.clean: The DNS this computer uses ({servers}) is not affected by the DNS block, so DNS alone would not stop you; the other layers matter.
connect.noIps: No usable IP addresses to test.
control.noConnectivity: No connectivity to {host}:{port} ({outcome}); results would be meaningless.
tcp.reset: TCP connections are reset on every IP: IP-level block.
tcp.timeout: TCP connections time out on every IP: probably an IP-level block, but a down server looks the same without an outside check.
tcp.partial: TCP is blocked on {blocked} of {total} IPs only; not counted as an IP block.
tls.sni: The TLS handshake dies with SNI "{host}" but succeeds with "{alt}" on the same IP: SNI/DPI block.
tls.anySni: TLS fails whatever the SNI on some IP: a server problem or IP-level filtering, not attributable to SNI.
http.blockPage: Plain HTTP on {ip} returned a block page ({signature}).
ref.reachable: Reachable from outside ({provider}): the host is up, so the failures seen here are not an outage.
ref.unreachable: Also unreachable from outside ({provider}): the host is most likely down for everyone, not blocked.
throttle.detected: Throttled: {real} with SNI "{sni}" vs {control} for the control ({target}); ratio {ratio}.
throttle.none: Not throttled: {real} vs {control} for the control (ratio {ratio}).
throttle.reason.small: response too small to judge throughput ({bytes} bytes); point the target at a larger resource
throttle.reason.window: download window too short to measure
throttle.reason.noControl: no usable control measurement (the server rejects the SNI swap and the external controls failed)
throttle.reason.slowControl: the control itself is too slow ({bps} B/s); the connection is slow
env.vpn: A VPN/tunnel seems active (traffic leaves through {iface}). Blocks are applied by your ISP, so blocked sites may look accessible. Turn the VPN off for a true result.
env.hotspot: You seem to be on a phone hotspot ({kind}). Mobile operators apply blocks their own way and Turkish ISP DNS servers may not answer; results describe the mobile network.
wizard.title: trblocked setup
wizard.hint: Use the arrow keys and Enter
wizard.reference.q: Confirm suspected IP blocks from outside Turkey? (sends only the hostname to api.globalping.io, and only when needed)
wizard.warnings.q: Warn me when a VPN or phone hotspot may distort the results?
wizard.none: No saved settings yet. Run: trblocked config
help: Usage: trblocked <url|host|ip>... [options]
trblocked config [show]
Checks whether hosts are blocked in Turkey and how: dns, ip, sni, http, throttle.
Options:
-f, --file <path>      read targets from a file, one per line ("-" = stdin; # comments allowed)
-c, --concurrency <n>  targets checked in parallel (default 16)
--throttle         also measure bandwidth throttling (downloads a few MB, one target at a time)
--injection        repeat plain-HTTP requests to catch block pages that DPI injects only some of the time
--no-reference     do not confirm suspected IP blocks from outside Turkey
(default: on; sends only the hostname to api.globalping.io, only when needed)
--lang <tr|en>     output language (see: trblocked config)
--ascii            force plain ASCII output (Turkish letters transliterated); --unicode forces UTF-8
--config <file>    JSON file overriding config/default.json
--json             machine-readable output on stdout
-v, --verbose          show every note for every target
-s, --silent           only results: no progress display, no warnings
--no-color         disable colors (NO_COLOR is honored too)
--no-progress      disable the live progress display
-V, --version          show the version
-h, --help             show this help
trblocked config        interactive setup (language, outside check, warnings)
Progress is drawn on stderr and cleared when done; results go to stdout.
Exit codes: 0 all accessible, 1 something blocked, 2 inconclusive / error / usage
